newsitem.title: USA: AOL suffers a brief email outage.
newsitem.headline: AOL suffers a brief email outage.

text.p: America Online Inc said that it suffered an outage earlier Thursday that prevented its eight million plus members from accessing their electronic mail for over an hour.
A spokeswoman said that AOL had to replace a board in one of its servers that manages electronic mail. The server went down at 1230 EST/1730 GMT, she said, and it was back up by 1340 EST/1840 GMT.
The Dulles, Va.-based company has been beset with network problems every since it switched its members over to unlimited usage for a flat rate of $19.95 a month on December 1.

The AOL spokeswoman later said AOL also suffered from an email outage earlier Thursday, from about 0715 EST/1215 GMT to 0915 EST/1415 GMT, due to a power supply problem. "There were two different things," the spokeswoman said. She said AOL shut down its system down from 0500 EST/1000 GMT to 0700 EST/1200 GMT to increase the hardware capacity overnight. After the system came back up, an email problem email began at 0715/1215 GMT. Members could not access mail for two hours in the morning and again from 1230 EST/1730 GMT to 1340 EST/1840 GMT.
The problems with AOL's electronic mail servers come on the heels of an almost four hour partial outage last week.

At the same time, attorneys general from 20 states were meeting in Chicago on Thursday to respond to the tide of consumer complaints about America Online. Some states said last week that they were receiving customer complaints about how they cannot access the service, especially during peak usage hours. AOL did not have an immediate comment.

The Dulles, Va.-based company was also hit with at least four class action lawsuits last week, filed on behalf of all members. The allegations in the suits against AOL range from false advertising to breach of contract, saying AOL is not providing the unlimited access to its service that it promised.
